title: Dhurandhar Opens Indian Panorama as IFFI Goa Unveils 2026 Programme
excerpt: The 57th International Film Festival of India runs in Goa from November 20 to 28, with Ramayana opening the BRICS segment and The Kerala Story 2: Goes Beyond in the International Competition.
body:
• The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) runs in Goa from November 20 to 28, 2026, under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, screening 159 international films from 86 countries.
  • The Hindi feature Dhurandhar and the Ladakhi-language non-feature Becoming will open the Indian Panorama, which presents 76 films in 18 languages.
  • India's Ramayana will open a special BRICS segment, and The Kerala Story 2: Goes Beyond is listed in the International Competition, according to Bollywood Hungama, citing IFFI's social media announcement.
  • Planning to attend? Screenings run across 13 indoor screens in Panaji, Porvorim, Margao and Ponda over the nine days from November 20.

The programme for the 57th International Film Festival of India was unveiled at a curtain-raiser press conference in Goa on November 13, inaugurated by Goa Chief Minister Dr Pramod Sawant. The festival, held from November 20 to 28, 2026, received more than 1,900 film submissions from 137 countries and will showcase 159 international films representing 86 countries, alongside 76 Indian films. Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker said the theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, reflects cinema's ability to connect audiences across geographical, linguistic and cultural boundaries. The full announcement was covered by Bollywood Hungama.

The festival itself opens with Fatherland, directed by Paweł Pawlikowski, which follows Nobel laureate Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika travelling through post-war, divided Germany in 1949. The film received the Best Director Award at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The mid-festival film is I Matter, directed by Alina Șerban, a 101-minute co-production of Romania, Germany and Belgium with dialogue in Romanian and Romani. Singapore's We Are All Strangers, directed by Anthony Chen and presented in Mandarin and English, will close the festival.

Indian Panorama and the BRICS spotlight

The Indian Panorama will open with Dhurandhar, a Hindi feature film directed by Aditya Dhar and starring Ranveer Singh, and Becoming, a Ladakhi-language non-feature film. The section presents 76 films in 18 languages, selected after the festival received 404 feature-film submissions and 358 non-feature submissions; the Best Web Series (OTT) category received 46 eligible entries. Titles named in the Panorama selection include Kantara: A Legend Chapter – 1 and The Kerala Story 2: Goes Beyond.

IFFI 2026 places a special focus on BRICS cinema. India's Ramayana will be the opening film of the BRICS segment, which will showcase films from all 11 member countries along with contributions from partner countries.

Country showcases and new segments

Spain is this year's Country of Honour, with four films: The Bad Son, directed by Jaime Lorente; Trinidad; Bitter Christmas, directed by Pedro Almodóvar; and Persegiuiendo a Michael, directed by Jaime Machia. Russia is the Partner Country, also presenting four films, including Four, New Home, Bo Bo, directed by Anastasia Kuzina, and Sidney Lumet's Birthday. The Gala Premieres segment will feature 14 screenings.

Two new segments debut this year. Animation will present five films, and Films About Films will also present five, a section the festival says was introduced in response to suggestions from filmmakers to bring the craft of filmmaking to the forefront. The programme will also bring together 52 women filmmakers, and the sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow will select 100 participants across 13 filmmaking crafts.

Competition, tributes and what's next

According to Bollywood Hungama, citing a video posted on IFFI's social media handles, The Kerala Story 2: Goes Beyond is among the films in the International Competition — a separate listing from its place in the Indian Panorama programme. The festival's competitive sections also include the Best Debut Feature Film Competition, which will feature seven films from across the world.

IFFI 2026 will mark the birth centenaries of filmmakers Shakti Samanta and Raj Khosla, actors Uttam Kumar, Suryakant Mandhare, Prem Nazir and Raj Kumar, and music composers O. P. Nayyar and Ravi. A tribute to the late Nana Patekar is planned with an open-sky screening of Natsamrat (2016) at Miramar Beach, according to Bollywood Hungama. Beyond the screenings, Kala Academy will host 14 sessions from November 21 to 27, and the WAVES Film Bazaar will connect filmmakers with producers, buyers and distributors. For diaspora audiences following Indian cinema from abroad, the Panorama's 18-language slate — opening with a Hindi feature and a Ladakhi non-feature on the same platform — is the clearest statement of this year's theme.
